summary: SSE client send-window exhaustion causes late KV-cache priming and partial/duplicated output on resume
description:
Issue summary: Customers are observing partial or duplicated final tokens when an SSE stream resumes after a short period of client-side send-window exhaustion (client cannot send ACKs/heartbeats due to local buffer pressure). Impact: user-facing partial responses, occasionally duplicated prefix fragments on resume. Occurs intermittently for long-running streams (>30s) behind aggressive client-side upload/backpressure and certain proxy buffering configurations.

Impact: Several NovaForms customers reported truncated form-fill instructions and duplicated opening sentences when their webapp regains connectivity after a short spike in outgoing data (WS/SSE heartbeat/analytics). This leads to confusing or malformed outputs in production workflows.

What we suspect: when the client send-window is exhausted the client's outbound control frames (keepalive/ack) are delayed. On reconnect the service attempts to apply KV cache priming based on last session markers, but the priming messages are delayed or arrive after initial incremental tokens, producing interleaved fragments or missing the terminal metadata that marks completion.

Observed frequency: ~2% of streams for the customer under high client-side telemetry; reproducible in canary by simulating a 200–500ms blocked client-send window during streaming.

Customer contact: product-support@novaforms.example (CS rep: Lara Kim).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long SSE generation request (>40s expected output) against redwood-2-small in prod-us-east using NovaForms web client configuration.
2) Simulate client-side outbound congestion: throttle or pause the browser's fetch/write loop for 200–500ms (serviceworker or large analytics burst), causing send-window exhaustion.
3) Allow the client to resume sending (unpause). Observe the SSE stream reassembly in the client and transcript in logs.

4) Repeat 10–20 times. Failure observed in ~1–3 runs for our setup: either (A) final paragraph missing, (B) duplicated opening sentence, or (C) interleaved metadata control chunk appearing mid-output.
Notes: Reproduction is more reliable with an intermediate reverse proxy configured with aggressive buffer and http2 windowing (nginx default plus proxy_buffering on).
Tested with client-sdk v1.9.2 and v1.10.0-canary; canary shows slightly better behavior but not eliminated.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-08): reproduced in-house using a headless chrome harness that pauses the ServiceWorker outgoing queue for 250ms. Observed two failure modes: duplicated opening fragment (priming applied after initial incremental tokens) and missing terminal metadata (priming overwrote terminal marker path).

Hypothesis A: api-gateway treats resumed connections as in-order but priming is queued on a separate low-priority channel; if priming arrives late it is stitched after live tokens leading to duplication.

Hypothesis B: client-side reconstructor assumes all priming arrives before first token after resume; if the client send-window is exhausted, control frames for 'ack/resume' are batched leading to a race.

SRE test (2026-03-09): instrumented a short-path within api-gateway to apply priming synchronously on resume for a small percentage of traffic for NovaForms. Duplication rate dropped from ~2% to ~0.3% during canary. This indicates ordering is the main factor.
Investigated nginx proxy buffering: with proxy_buffering on, late priming is more frequent (buffer flush alignment). With proxy_buffering disabled reproduction rate lowered.

Client SDK review: v1.9.2 reconstruction expects 'priming' control event before tokens; v1.10.0-canary tolerates late priming by merging fragments if terminal meta present, but still misses cases where terminal meta is dropped.

resolution: Workaround: recommend NovaForms upgrade to client-sdk v1.10.0-canary and avoid large client-side outbound bursts during active SSE streams.
Short-term mitigation: deployed api-gateway canary that applies priming synchronously on resume for affected customer; reduced duplication from ~2% to ~0.3%.

Long-term fix: implement ordering guard in the resume codepath of api-gateway to ensure KV priming control frames are committed before any subsequent user tokens are emitted. Additional unit tests to simulate client send-window exhaustion will be added to e2e harness.
Follow-ups: coordinate release of serving-runtime ordering guard (PR #4242) and client-sdk stable release (PR #998), then monitor NovaForms production for 7 days after full rollout.
